approach: Add one path function, `paths::records_worktree(state_dir)` (`<state>/records-worktree`), beside `repo_state_dir`. Add `RecordSet::load_dir` and `RecordSet::load_current(git, treeish, worktree)` in athena-gate. `load_current` reads `<worktree>/records/**` through `check_record_file` when `worktree.is_dir()`, else calls `RecordSet::load`. Add `Records::load_current(git, treeish, worktree)` in store.rs the same way, using `Records::load_dir` (records/ half from `RecordSet::load_dir`, landings/ from the worktree). Its doc comment says landings come only from the worktree's `landings/`, not merged with the branch tip as `Records::load` does. Switch exactly three call sites: `Athena::status` (two loads), which also feeds `class_forecasts`, and `Athena::land_pr`'s job lookup. Add tests that use distinct job ids in the worktree and in-tree records/. Add a new §14 to records-history.md listing every remaining reader by file and function. The search widens to `JobFiles::load(`, `ls_tree_under(` on records/ and landings/ paths, and the file readers. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Probe the worktree first with `Path::is_dir()`; if it exists use it even when empty; read records/ from the treeish only when the directory is absent.
decisions.reason: The request says 'only when the worktree is absent'. A broken or empty worktree must not hide behind frozen in-tree records.

rejected.option: Fall back when the worktree has no records/ or fails to parse
rejected.why: Hides a broken worktree behind stale records, which D111 moves away from.

decisions.choice: `paths::records_worktree(state_dir: &Path) -> PathBuf` returns `state_dir.join("records-worktree")`; the loaders take the worktree path as an argument.
decisions.reason: The literal is defined once. Tests control the location through the `StateDir` they already pass to `Athena`, with no global environment variable. `state.rs` is not a deliverable, so no wrapper is added.

rejected.why: Test `Athena` instances use `StateDir::new(temp)` and never reach that path; tests would need the global `ATHENA_STATE_DIR`.
`state.rs` is not in the deliverables; three call sites do not justify a wrapper.

decisions.choice: Add `RecordSet::load_dir(dir)` in athena-gate and make `Records::load_dir` use it for the records/ half.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-gate, not the reverse, so the gate crate needs its own filesystem loader. Sharing it keeps one copy of the check-and-wrap code. The test at status.rs ~2820-2853 (load vs load_dir) keeps guarding equivalence.

rejected.option: Build the set via a temporary git index
rejected.why: Needs git state for a plain directory; the worktree may be dirty.

decisions.choice: Landings in `Records::load_current` with a worktree come only from `<worktree>/landings`, not merged with the live tip of the local records branch as `Records::load` does via `landing_files` (store.rs 290-296). This is stated in the doc comment and in §14.
decisions.reason: The worktree is a checkout of the branch, so its landings/ is the branch's landings once it is at the tip. §13 already requires the worktree to be 'updated to the branch tip before a read'. That duty belongs to the writer slice, which is out of scope. Merging `RecordsWriter::tip` landings would make the 'worktree is the source' rule unclear and would hide a stale worktree.

rejected.option: Also call `landing_files(git, treeish)` and merge the tip's landings
rejected.why: Reads the branch beside the worktree, so a test with distinct ids could not show the worktree is the only source, and a lagging worktree would be hidden.

decisions.choice: The moved 'forecast' is the per-class forecast headline in `athena status`: `class_forecasts(&records)` (status.rs 794, called ~1098) over the one `records` value loaded by `Records::load_current`. No separate loader.
decisions.reason: Two sources inside one status call would be wrong. The reference forecaster (`scoring::reference` and `history` called from reading.rs ~583 and ~779 over `Records::load`) is a different reader and stays; §14 and the CHANGELOG say so.

rejected.option: A separate load for the forecast
rejected.why: Two sources inside one status call.

rejected.option: Move the reading.rs reference forecaster too
rejected.why: Out of scope: only status, the forecast headline and land_pr's lookup move.

decisions.choice: The land_pr test uses the lookup's own outcome as evidence. A job found in the source gives 'has no verification'; an unknown job gives 'no job matches'. A no-origin repository and an always-erroring `Runner` keep the host out of it.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` calls `reconcile`, which does not fail and returns early with no `origin` remote. It then resolves the job and checks its verification before it touches the remote. No host fake is needed.

rejected.why: Pulls in remotes and CI state that are out of scope for a lookup test.

decisions.choice: The status test asserts job ids over the union of `view.open` and `view.recent` (and `jobs_by_state` total), not over `open` alone.
decisions.reason: `scan_jobs` (status.rs 911-950) puts only jobs whose `state_name` is 'queued' outside `recent`, and `open` holds queued and other open states. The id is compared across both lists, so the test does not depend on which state a Request-only fixture gets. The fixture still asserts the state name it observes.

rejected.why: Fails for the wrong reason if the fixture's state is not open.

risks.risk: A worktree that exists but is empty or partly written makes status and land_pr see no jobs, with no fallback.
risks.mitigation: This is the chosen rule. Production creates no worktree in this slice. §14 says the writer slice must create the directory only once it is complete. A unit test covers the empty-directory case.

risks.risk: A worktree lagging the branch tip hides recent landings, because `load_current` reads only `<worktree>/landings` and does not merge the tip's landings as `Records::load` does.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and §14 state this. §13 already requires the worktree to be updated to the branch tip before a read; the writer slice owns that. No worktree exists in production yet.

risks.risk: Until later slices move the other readers, status and land_pr could disagree with commands that still read HEAD.
risks.mitigation: The worktree does not exist in production yet. §14 lists the remaining readers and the CHANGELOG says only these moved.

risks.risk: Refactoring `Records::load_dir` could change file order or paths for snapshot users.
risks.mitigation: `RecordSet::load_dir` yields the same relative '/' paths sorted by path. The status.rs load-vs-load_dir test, snapshot.rs tests and gate_counts.rs tests guard it.

risks.risk: The forecast test's fixtures could fail `check_record_file` and land in `invalid`, so the test passes or fails for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: Each record is built as a typed `AnyRecord` and written at `canonical_path()` with `to_json()`. The test asserts `view.invalid_records` is empty for each source.

risks.risk: The §14 list is long and could miss a reader, since the Greps are on call patterns.
risks.mitigation: The criterion 6 command lists the exact patterns the verifier re-runs (`Records::load(`, `RecordSet::load(`, `GitRecords::load(`, `JobFiles::load(`, records-path `ls_tree_under(`, `read_files_under(`, records-path `read_dir(`). The producer reads each hit's enclosing fn.

demonstrations.method: Three tests with 'records_worktree' in the name. status.rs has a status test and a forecast test; gh/tests.rs has a land_pr test. Each is built on `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()`. Each commits one job into in-tree records/ with `athena.commit_records`. It writes a different job's typed `AnyRecord` files (`canonical_path()`, `to_json()`) under `paths::records_worktree(athena.state.root())`. Status test: `Athena::status()`, assert the worktree job id is in `open`+`recent`, the in-tree id is in neither, and `invalid_records` is empty. Forecast test: the worktree job has class `class-wt` with a Score and the in-tree job has `class-tree` with a Score; assert `view.forecasts` has `class-wt` and not `class-tree`. Land_pr test: `athena.land_pr(<worktree id>, &ErrRunner, Poll{attempts:1, delay:Duration::ZERO, sleep:&|_|{}}, &Quiet)` fails with 'has no verification' and `land_pr(<in-tree id>, ...)` fails with 'no job matches'.
demonstrations.observes: All three pass: with the worktree present, each reader sees only the worktree's job ids and class.
demonstrations.fails_without: If status, the forecast or land_pr still used `Records::load` on the treeish, the worktree ids would be missing from `open`+`recent`, `forecasts` would show `class-tree`, and land_pr of the worktree job would fail with 'no job matches'.

Fixture `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()` (exists, code_health.rs ~1065) gives a temp git repo and temp `StateDir`. The worktree is injected by writing files under `paths::records_worktree(state.root())`, which plan step 1 adds. The `Runner` is a small test type whose `gh` returns Err; it holds no logic under test and is not reached (no origin remote, lookup fails first). `Runner` exists (gh/transport.rs ~13).

demonstrations.method: The same three tests run a second half: `std::fs::remove_dir_all(paths::records_worktree(state.root()))`, then the same entry points. Unit tests in store.rs and gate records.rs: `load_current` with a nonexistent worktree path equals `load(git, "HEAD")` for the same repo; with an existing worktree it equals `load_dir`; an existing empty directory gives no records and does not fall back.
